Loading and cleaning the data

Sources: - Macroeconomic predictors: https://www.stevanovic.uqam.ca/DS_LCMD.html - Canadian CPI: https://www150.statcan.gc.ca/t1/tbl1/en/tv.action?pid=1810000401 (check at 8:30pm) - FRED-MD data: https://www.stlouisfed.org/research/economists/mccracken/fred-databases

References:

Fortin-Gagnon, O., Leroux, M., Stevanovic, D. and Surprenant, S. (2022), A large Canadian database for macroeconomic analysis. Canadian Journal of Economics/Revue canadienne d’économique, 55: 1799-1833. https://doi.org/10.1111/caje.12618

Statistics Canada. Table 18-10-0004-01 Consumer Price Index, monthly, not seasonally adjusted. DOI: https://doi.org/10.25318/1810000401-eng

Data is obtained from:

August 2026 zip file downloaded from the data source

readme.txt content:

These files contain datasets used in: Fortin-Gagnon, Leroux, Stevanovic and Surprenant (2018) A Large Canadian Data for Macroeconomic Analysis.

  • CAN_MD.xlsx: raw data as collected from StatCan. It starts from 1914 because the CPI series is available from that year
  • TR_CAN_MD.xlsx: data from CAN_MD.xlsx transformed to induce stationarity.
  • balanced_can_md.xlsx: stationary and balanced panel starting from 1981M01. Missing values are replaced by EM algorithm.
  • Table_can_md.xlsx: detailed data description

We use balanced_can_md.xlsx as the data is already stationary and balanced panel.

From Table_can_md.xlsx we can see that the following variables are discontinued and ends in September 2020. we should remove these from the data source - CRED_T-discontinued - CRED_HOURS_discontinued - CRED_MORT_discontinued - CRED_CONS_discontinued - CRED_BUS_discontinued

Keeping track of the variables

  • can_md: Macroeconomic data. 1981-01-01 to 2026-07-01
    • Note: variables have been prefixed with “CAN_” in case there are overlaps with FRED data
  • cpi_model_self: CPI (not officially seasonally adjusted, self adjusted using ARIMA). 1981-01-01 to 2026-07-01
    • Note: variables have been prefixed with “US_” in case there are overlaps with CAN data
  • cpi_model_official: CPI (officially seasonally adjusted). 1992-01-01 to 2026-07-01
  • fred_md: FRED data. 1981-01-01 to 2026-07-01

Outputs (RDS)

Outputs have merged the variables into the following - main_data_self.rds = can_md + cpi_model_self - main_data_official.rds = can_md + cpi_model_official - extended_data_self.rds = can_md + cpi_model_self + fred_md - extended_data_official.rds = can_md + cpi_model_official + fred_md

## [1] 350
# check duplicates 
sum(duplicated(can_md$Date))
## [1] 0
range(can_md$Date)
## [1] "1981-01-01" "2026-07-01"
# check date range, if every month is present
nrow(can_md)
## [1] 547
expected_dates <- seq(
  min(can_md$Date),
  max(can_md$Date),
  by = "month"
)
setdiff(expected_dates, can_md$Date)
## Date of length 0
discontinued_vars <- c(
  "CRED_T_discontinued",
  "CRED_HOUS_discontinued",
  "CRED_MORT_discontinued",
  "CRED_CONS_discontinued",
  "CRE_BUS_discontinued"
)

intersect(discontinued_vars, names(can_md))
## [1] "CRED_T_discontinued"    "CRED_HOUS_discontinued" "CRED_MORT_discontinued"
## [4] "CRED_CONS_discontinued" "CRE_BUS_discontinued"
can_md <- can_md %>%
  select(-any_of(discontinued_vars))

# check whether removed
sum(is.na(can_md))
## [1] 0
# rename variables to standardise across datasets
can_md <- can_md %>%
  rename(date = Date) %>%
  mutate(date = as.Date(date)) %>%
  arrange(date) %>% 
  rename_with(
    ~ paste0("CAN_", .x),
    -date
  )

CPI Data

Testing unseasonally adjusted data -> ARIMA adjustment -> compare against officially seasonally adjusted data. Unsure of which one to use…

# import canadian CPI data
cpi_raw <- read_csv("data/raw/1810000401_databaseLoadingData.csv",
                    show_col_types = FALSE)
cpi_official_raw <- read_csv("data/raw/1810000601_databaseLoadingData.csv",
                    show_col_types = FALSE)
# clean column headers

Since the data cpi is not seasonally adjusted, we use X-13ARIMA-SEATS to seasonally adjust.

# check for regularly spaced time series
cpi_ts <- ts(
  cpi$cpi,
  start = c(
    year(min(cpi$date)),
    month(min(cpi$date))
  ),
  frequency = 12
)

start(cpi_ts)
## [1] 1981    1
end(cpi_ts)
## [1] 2026    7
frequency(cpi_ts)
## [1] 12
# to seasonally adjust our CPI, we use ARIMA
# Estimate seasonal adjustment
sa_model <- seas(
  cpi_ts,
  x11 = ""
)

# Extract seasonally adjusted CPI
cpi_sa <- final(sa_model)

# Examine model
summary(sa_model)
## 
## Call:
## seas(x = cpi_ts, x11 = "")
## 
## Coefficients:
##                   Estimate Std. Error z value Pr(>|z|)    
## LS1991.Jan        0.022606   0.002922   7.736 1.03e-14 ***
## MA-Nonseasonal-01 0.913886   0.017144  53.306  < 2e-16 ***
## MA-Seasonal-12    0.868727   0.022387  38.806  < 2e-16 ***
## ---
## Signif. codes:  0 '***' 0.001 '**' 0.01 '*' 0.05 '.' 0.1 ' ' 1
## 
## X11 adj.  ARIMA: (0 2 1)(0 1 1)  Obs.: 547  Transform: log
## AICc: 305.7, BIC: 322.8  QS (no seasonality in final):    0  
## Box-Ljung (no autocorr.): 26.96   Shapiro (normality): 0.9853 ***
# Plot results
plot(sa_model)

cpi_adjusted <- data.frame(
  date = cpi$date,
  cpi_unadjusted = cpi$cpi,
  cpi_adjusted = as.numeric(cpi_sa)
)
# we observe the performance of self adjusted CPI
comparison <- cpi_adjusted %>%
  inner_join(cpi_official, by = "date")

range(comparison$date)
## [1] "1992-01-01" "2026-07-01"
nrow(comparison)
## [1] 415
# plot self-adjusted and officially adjusted
comparison_long <- comparison %>%
  select(date, cpi_adjusted, cpi_official) %>%
  pivot_longer(
    cols = -date,
    names_to = "series",
    values_to = "cpi"
  )

ggplot(comparison_long,
       aes(x = date, y = cpi, color = series)) +
  geom_line(linewidth = 0.7) +
  labs(
    title = "Comparison of Seasonally Adjusted Canadian CPI",
    x = "Year",
    y = "CPI Index",
    color = "Series"
  ) +
  theme_minimal()

# compare inflation rates
comparison <- comparison %>%
  arrange(date) %>%
  mutate(
    inflation_self =
      1200 * (log(cpi_adjusted) -
              log(lag(cpi_adjusted))),

    inflation_official =
      1200 * (log(cpi_official) -
              log(lag(cpi_official)))
  )

ggplot(comparison, aes(x = date)) +
  geom_line(
    aes(y = inflation_self, color = "Self-adjusted")
  ) +
  geom_line(
    aes(y = inflation_official, color = "Official")
  ) +
  labs(
    title = "Monthly Inflation: Self-adjusted vs Official",
    x = "Year",
    y = "Annualised Inflation (%)",
    color = "Series"
  ) +
  theme_minimal()
## Warning: Removed 1 row containing missing values or values outside the scale range
## (`geom_line()`).
## Removed 1 row containing missing values or values outside the scale range
## (`geom_line()`).

# quantitative analysis
valid <- comparison %>%
  filter(
    !is.na(inflation_self),
    !is.na(inflation_official)
  )

errors <- valid$inflation_self -
          valid$inflation_official

mae <- mean(abs(errors))
rmse <- sqrt(mean(errors^2))
bias <- mean(errors)

correlation <- cor(
  valid$inflation_self,
  valid$inflation_official
)

data.frame(
  MAE = mae,
  RMSE = rmse,
  Bias = bias,
  Correlation = correlation
)

Constructing our target

Metric following Mederios et al., who forecast: 1. Monthly inflation at future month+h (h=1,2,…,12) 2. Accumulated inflation over next h months (h=3,6,12)

head(cpi_adjusted)
##         date cpi_unadjusted cpi_adjusted
## 1 1981-01-01           46.9     47.09816
## 2 1981-02-01           47.4     47.50002
## 3 1981-03-01           48.0     47.99336
## 4 1981-04-01           48.3     48.33372
## 5 1981-05-01           48.7     48.77688
## 6 1981-06-01           49.5     49.31330
head(cpi_official)
## # A tibble: 6 × 2
##   date       cpi_official
##   <date>            <dbl>
## 1 1992-01-01         83.1
## 2 1992-02-01         83.2
## 3 1992-03-01         83.6
## 4 1992-04-01         83.7
## 5 1992-05-01         83.9
## 6 1992-06-01         84.1

Columns: - date - cpi - log_cpi - inflation_mom (historical monthly inflation) - inflation_12m - target_h1 (1-month-ahead forecasting) - target_h3 (3-month-ahead forecasting) - target_h6 (6-month-ahead forecasting) - target_h12 (12-month-ahead forecasting) - accumulated_h3 (realised 3-month accumulated inflation) - accumulated_h6 (realised 6-month accumulated inflation) - accumulated_h12 (realised 12-month accumulated inflation)

construct_inflation <- function(data, cpi_col) {
  data %>%
    arrange(date) %>%
    transmute(
      date,
      cpi = {{ cpi_col }},
      log_cpi = log(cpi),

      # historical inflation
      inflation_mom = log_cpi - lag(log_cpi),
      inflation_12m = log_cpi - lag(log_cpi, 12)
    ) %>%
    mutate(
      # future monthly inflation
      target_h1 = lead(inflation_mom, 1),
      target_h3 = lead(inflation_mom, 3),
      target_h6 = lead(inflation_mom, 6),
      target_h12 = lead(inflation_mom, 12),

      # future accumulated inflation
      accumulated_h3 = lead(log_cpi, 3) - log_cpi,
      accumulated_h6 = lead(log_cpi, 6) - log_cpi,
      accumulated_h12 = lead(log_cpi, 12) - log_cpi
    )
}

# self adjusted seasonality
cpi_model_self <- construct_inflation(cpi_adjusted, cpi_adjusted)

# officially adjusted
cpi_model_official <- construct_inflation(cpi_official, cpi_official)
